target_customer: Hospitals and surgical teams (perioperative and critical care monitoring), plus sleep researchers
problem: Continuous blood pressure monitoring normally needs an invasive arterial line or intermittent cuffs. Vena Vitals makes a cuffless adhesive sensor that tracks beat-by-beat pressure at lower cost and with less risk.
business_model: Regulated medical device sold to hospitals and research customers; not yet commercially sold pending FDA 510(k) review
product_category: Wearable cuffless blood pressure sensor (medical device)

education: BS Electrical Engineering, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
previous_startups: Two prior health tech exits, to Cigna and Vizient (per YC page; which startup went to which buyer is not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page says 15+ years of leadership at GE Healthcare, Siemens and startups, and that he set up a factory quality system in China that passed FDA inspection.

founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC company page; no role or employers given there.

competitors.name: Aktiia
competitors.what: Swiss cuffless optical bracelet for continuous blood pressure, pursuing FDA clearance and CE mark
competitors.traction_then: Algorithm validated in clinical trials against arterial lines; 15 employees; in final steps before market
competitors.funding_then: CHF 4M seed (2018) plus USD 6.1M round led by Redalpine (reported March 2020)

technical_complexity.rationale: A thin adhesive sensor that matches arterial-line accuracy needs novel nanomaterial sensing, clinical validation in operating rooms and FDA clearance. This is hardware and regulatory heavy work for a nine-person team.

defensibility.rationale: University-derived sensor technology plus the need for FDA clearance and clinical data raise the bar, but several funded cuffless approaches (for example Aktiia) pursued the same goal with different physics.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying by incumbents found. As of 2026 sources the company was still pre-clearance with a 510(k) submitted or being prepared.

market_need_then: Arterial lines are invasive and cuffs give only intermittent readings, so surgeons and sleep researchers lack cheap continuous pressure data. The company reports operating room comparisons against arterial lines on its site; the numbers there could not be verified.

branding.domain_note: Uses venavitals.com (exact name .com); no purchase history found.

identity.logo: Wordmark styled VENAVITALS with a macron over the E per a March 2025 trademark filing

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself, no community or merch found. The name is descriptive and the brand is a minor factor for a regulated device sold to hospitals.

outcome_analysis: Vena Vitals is still active and pre-commercial. It spun out of a UC Irvine lab, joined YC in Summer 2020 and has relied on a small seed plus NIH and NSF grants and accelerators. Its path depends on FDA 510(k) clearance for the VeriTrack sensor, and no shutdown, acquisition or layoffs were found. Funding figures across aggregators conflict, so its true runway is unclear.
notes: Funding is unclear. MTEC lists a $3.6M seed announced 2020-09-15 and seedtable lists a seed dated 2020-08. Sig.ai (aggregator) claims $10M in 2024, Caplight lists a 2025 seed with total $3.12M, and Standout lists $225K total; these are unverified and not recorded as rounds. UCI coverage says funding is a mix of venture and federal grants (NIH SBIR, NSF). Biobeat was named as an Aktiia rival in a 2020-era MobiHealthNews piece but that page could not be opened to confirm its date, so it is not listed. Founder roles beyond the YC page are only partly sourced.
